answer: Each epoch, agents must answer a challenge word drawn from a public randomness beacon, e.g. trellis, tundra, or echo, woven into a short live reasoning task. Since the word is unknowable before the beacon reveals it, an attacker cannot precompute template replies across thousands of fake identities; every sybil must actually run a model per identity per epoch. That turns cheap mass registration into a real per-agent compute and latency cost, so faking N identities costs roughly N times honest operation, collapsing the sybil economics.
